messages:
support_jen: Pasting a customer report — they're hitting repeated parse failures in JSON mode after switching to the newer inference runtime. Customer sees partial objects inside arrays (some items missing required 'id'), plus extra transient keys like 'temp_id' and ordering assumptions being violated. Also saw a billing spike. Asking for quick triage: can someone help repro and check whether this is model output drift vs server-side stream splitting?

support_jen: Customer's minimal repro (they say they used our /v1/generate structured_output):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "model": "open-variant-2b",
    "prompt": "Produce JSON array of order objects. Each item MUST have id, product_id, qty. No extra fields.",
    "structured_output": {"mode": "json_mode", "schema": "items[]:{id:string,product_id:string,qty:int}"},
    "stream": false
  }'
```

support_jen: Customer's actual response (trimmed):
```json
[
  {"product_id":"sku-123","qty":2},
  {"id":"ord-2","product_id":"sku-5","qty":1},
  {"id":"ord-3","product_id":"sku-9","qty":4,"temp_id":"t-987"},
  {"product_id":"sku-2","qty":1,"id":"ord-4"}
]
```

support_jen: Notes: first item missing id, third item has extra temp_id, ordering not stable (customer expects stream-order == original). They said parser fails on first item and they retried multiple times which inflated tokens billed.

eng_marc: :eyes: Thanks. A few quick checks: 1) confirm whether the response was streamed then reassembled client-side (streaming can cut mid-object) 2) check model variant and runtime (open-variant-2b vs open-variant-2b-quant) 3) request_id + raw response from our ingress logs. Can you paste request_id/ts from the customer logs?

support_jen: Request ids from customer logs: req_2026-08-05_07:31:12_a7c9 and req_2026-08-05_07:32:01_b12f. They attached the raw server response (we only have what they forwarded). I also pulled our proxy logs for req_2026-08-05_07:31:12_a7c9: ingress shows 200 and chunked transfer encoding, our runtime returned a sequence of frames: 
```
frame 1: "[\n  {\"product_id\":\"sku-123\",\"qty\":2},\n"
frame 2: "  {\"id\":\"ord-2\",...}\n"
frame 3: "  {\"id\":\"ord-3\",\"product_id\":...\n"
frame 4: "  {\"product_id\":\"sku-2\",\"qty\":1,\"id\":\"ord-4\"}\n]"
```

eng_maria: That looks like a classic stream-boundary truncation -> client reassembly might accidentally drop characters if it assumes each frame is JSON-safe. Two things: a) clients must concat frames exactly in order; b) our streaming layer should never split inside a token that breaks JSON tokens if possible. We recently shipped a micro-optimization that allows smaller frames for long arrays — could be related.

sre_lee: I'll lookup the deploy history for the streaming patch around that time. If the runtime chunker changed splitting behavior, we should see a correlate in deploy tags.

json-validator-bot: AUTOMATED CHECK: Provided response fails schema: missing required property 'id' on item[0]; additional property 'temp_id' present on item[2]; array item ordering differs from schema assumptions (schema doesn't prescribe order but client assumed stable ordering).

billing_sam: The customer reported 2x retries because of parser errors which doubled token spend. We should consider an emergency credit pending root cause. Can we get estimated tokens for those requests from logs?

support_jen: From token-log: req_...a7c9 = 18,432 tokens, req_...b12f = 18,450 tokens (they retried 2x each). They asked for a temporary hold on charges while we investigate.

eng_marc: Action plan (short):
- eng_marc: try to repro locally with same model + streaming on/off and with strict reassembly.
- sre_lee: confirm deploy/patches to streaming chunker at 2026-08-05 07:00 UTC window.
- eng_maria: if streaming frame splitting changed, add guard to not split inside JSON structural tokens OR include a frame boundary marker for clients to reassemble safely.
- billing_sam: please hold credits request pending root cause; we'll recommend a goodwill credit if it's our bug.

support_jen: Quick repro I ran: with streaming enabled, concatenating frames naively sometimes produced a leading object missing the id key when a bracket/brace got lost (client trimmed whitespace). Workaround for customer: set "stream": false or enforce client-side concatenation that doesn't strip whitespace. Also update prompts to include an explicit always-include id rule and emit objects in canonical order.

eng_marc: I'll run a controlled experiment with model=open-variant-2b and model=open-variant-2b-quant and with our pre/post-processing toggled. If I can reproduce server-side (same raw frames) it's an infra issue; if it only happens with a particular model variant, it's model generation/schema drift. Will report back in this thread.

billing_sam: Thanks. If infra is at fault, we'll apply a temporary credit for the affected requests. Please add exact request_ids to the billing ticket.

support_jen: Added ticket: BILL-5493 with req_...a7c9 and req_...b12f. Marking P1 for user impact (parser failures + billing). :white_check_mark:
